Customers dispute these incorrect charges, driving CRM dispute volume from 590 (Jul) to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) (E-03).

proposal.summary: Customer Service (SH-CS) requested an AI agent to auto-answer billing disputes and auto-fix wrong bills (CL-01), framing the doubling of dispute tickets since August as a response-speed problem. Investigation (PD-1) instead defined the root problem as a billing import validation rule change around August mis-processing normally-read (ACTUAL) bills, with a secondary contribution from a field route-completion shortfall; the release delivers only read-only diagnostic work (bill-charge analysis, route-completion verification, ticket-intake audit) with no automated bill writes or route changes, and is released WITH KNOWN LIMITATIONS because the critical rule-change confirmation step is still blocked.
key_points: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled from ~600/month (Jun/Jul) to 1180-1260/month (Aug/Sep 2026), confirming the surge SH-CS reported (E-03, CL-01).

Of disputed bills, more carry ACTUAL reads (1785) than ESTIMATED reads (1240, E-01), which weakens read-delivery/estimate-substitution as the dominant cause and points to a billing-side issue; no tariff change occurred (E-04, corroborated by E-06/CL-02).
Dispute ticket response times are within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d target, E-05), so SH-CS's response-speed framing (H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING) is not the bottleneck.

For disputed accounts, 1184 AMI reads arrived before cutoff and were exported to billing but rejected by billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, while only 56 had no AMI read at all (E-12); this rejects AMI-side delivery failure (H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE, status REJECTED) and supports a billing import validation rule mechanism (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE, status SUPPORTED).

Field manual-read route completion was 88% against a 95% target across 9200 accounts (E-02), with 14 specific lagging routes identified (E-10); this is treated as a secondary, partial contributor, not the dominant cause, per assumption A-FIELD-SHORTFALL-SECONDARY.

The release scope is limited to read-only diagnostic actions: analyze_disputed_bill_charges on DA-BILL, verify_field_route_completion on DA-ROUTE, and audit_dispute_ticket_intake on DA-TICKET (solution_design SD-1 release_scope); reviewing the billing rule-change log (DA-RULES) is excluded.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds; the DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, and the open verification obligation VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION (blocking review_billing_rule_change_log:DA-RULES) sits outside this release's scope.

Constraints enforced in the released scope: no automated writes to customer bills without Billing Operations authority (K-BILLWRITE), and any field dispatch route change requires runtime confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (K-DISPATCH, E-08).
limitations_explained: The DEFINE gate only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved before release.

VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION remains open and its blocking scope (reviewing the DA-RULES billing-config log) falls outside this release, so whether billing rules actually changed and which specific rule is at fault remains unresolved.
Even once identified, reverting or patching the mis-validating billing rule (SR-R3) is unfinished and must go through Billing Operations' own change-control process, not this release.
Whether dispute response times stay within the 3.0-day SLA throughout remediation is listed as an open/unfinished item, not something this release confirms going forward.
Because VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMATION blocks the DA-RULES review, H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE can be neither finally confirmed nor refuted within this release.

MDMS export access remains ACCESS_PENDING/NOT_TRANSIENT with no fallback (per recovery_decision seq 87), so the AMI-side contribution to the dispute surge (U-AMI-DATA-ACCESS) stays unresolved despite SH-AMI's unverified claim that access was provisioned (E-11/CL-04).

Stakeholder claims from SH-FIELD (E-07, staffing shortage) and SH-CS (CL-01, auto-fixable wrong bills) carry acknowledged bias (staffing-headcount incentive; response-speed framing bias) and were not independently corroborated within this release scope.
The billing-config tool's health is UNKNOWN, so even the deferred rule-log review may require retry or a fallback approach once the blocking VOB is cleared.
